request.spec:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests ran green.

**What changed (server only):**
- **`rollup/Rollup.java`**: each person's rollup figures now include their overdue-total. That is the sum of the dues on their overdue claims that count, worked out the same way as the `person-overdue-total` shown on screen. The sheet totals now include an overdue-total too, which adds up the people's rounded figures the same way the front end does. A person's ROLLUP line is now written when their overdue-total moves, even if their claimed and due-total didn't. A TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moves.
- **`SheetAudit.java`**: every ROLLUP line ends with `overdue-total=<…>`, and every TOTALS line ends with `overdue-total=<total>`. Both go after the existing fields, which stay in the same order.
- **`rollup/RollupChanged.java`**: comment updated to match.

Changing the sheet's today already went through the rollup check in `SheetService.setToday`. So a today change that puts a claim past its due-by now writes the rollup lines even when no due moved.

No front-end or stored-data changes were needed: the screen already showed overdue totals.
